slides.transcript:
HOW DID WE GET HERE?

Dwolla was started as a direct result of a problem encountered by its founder: the pain of paying $50,000+ a year in credit card fees. In 2008 Ben Milne set out to fix the problem and Dwolla was born.

Ben Milne, Founder & CEO
- Started his first manufacturing company at 18, bootstrapped the company to 1M + in revenue with operations in the US and Asia.
- Sold the company to concentrate on building the Dwolla network.
- Leads overall company vision, technology, product strategy and marketing.

Charise Flynn, COO
- Graduated magna cum laude from Simpson College with degrees in Philosophy and Religion.
- Started career in real estate development by building and managing over $100MM in real estate assets in less than five years.
- Built consulting company, c.Results, which focused on working with early stage companies/founders.
- Joined Dwolla in 2010 and leads operations including legal, finance, business development, human resources, and customer support.
slides.summary: This slide introduces the founding origin story of Dwolla and highlights the executive leadership team, detailing the background and operational experience of Founder & CEO Ben Milne and COO Charise Flynn.

slides.transcript:
THE PROBLEM WITH PAYMENTS

EXPENSIVE (“ASSET-HEAVY”)
• Merchants shell out ~$40-$50 billion a year to process credit/debit card payments. Does not include hardware, hidden fees, etc.
• Innovation can only happen on top of the network, which increases cost rather than reducing cost.
• Legacy payment options such as ACH and check are layered with administrative and operational costs that businesses, individuals, financial institutions and governments have to bear the cost of.
• Micro-transactions are cost-prohibitive.
SLOW/ACCESSIBILITY
• Check and ACH can take 3-15 days to get from senders’ to receivers’ bank account.
• Dependent on bank holidays, ATM availability
slides.summary: This slide highlights the pain points of current payment systems, focusing on high costs, asset-heavy structures, and slow transaction speeds. It details how traditional payment methods burden merchants, businesses, and individuals with excessive fees and lengthy settlement times.
key_points: Merchants pay ~$40-$50 billion annually to process credit and debit card payments, excluding hardware and hidden fees.
Innovation is restricted to the top of the network, increasing rather than reducing costs.
Legacy options like ACH and check involve heavy administrative, operational, and time costs (taking 3-15 days).
Micro-transactions are cost-prohibitive under current payment systems.
Traditional payment methods remain dependent on bank holidays and ATM availability.

slides.transcript:
THE PROBLEM WITH PAYMENTS

FRAUD HEAVY

• Credit and debit expose 16-digit card numbers, can be copied, photographed, or written down (i.e. “data exhaust”)

• Check and ACH expose info needed to make unauthorized debits to account, no inherent verification or validation protocols embedded in ACH

CLOSED & RIGID

• No inherently open payment network for third-party development, not Web 2.0-compatible

• Fragmented interests across spectrum, no true end-to-end solution in market

• Silo’d transaction combinations (e.g. cards are not p2p friendly, can’t use bank-to-bank networks to buy coffee)

BANK-CENTRIC

• Perpetuates increasingly regulated, endangered revenue streams for banks (see: Durbin Amendment, Bank of America checking fee backlash
slides.summary: This slide outlines the critical issues with existing payment infrastructures, categorizing them as fraud-heavy, closed and rigid, and bank-centric. It highlights vulnerabilities such as exposed 16-digit card numbers, lack of inherent verification in ACH, and fragmented, siloed networks that lack Web 2.0 compatibility and end-to-end solutions.
key_points: Credit and debit cards expose 16-digit numbers that can be copied or photographed.
Checks and ACH lack inherent verification protocols, enabling unauthorized debits.
Existing payment networks are closed, rigid, fragmented, and not Web 2.0-compatible.
Current transaction combinations are siloed and not friendly to peer-to-peer or everyday use cases like buying coffee.
The current system is bank-centric, perpetuating regulated and endangered revenue streams.

slides.transcript:
THE DWOLLA NETWORK

LOW COST “ASSET-LIGHT”
• Cuts expensive credit card fees out of the equation by bypassing existing card networks.
• $.25/transaction fee model is cheaper than credit cards or mailing/ processing check payments.
• Free micro-transactions (under $10) unlock new profit-making innovations, services, and markets
FAST/ACCESSIBLE
• Faster than mailing a check, pre-loaded funds move in real time
• FiSync Technology is first real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system in US
• Use with any web-enabled device
slides.summary: This slide outlines the Dwolla Network value proposition, highlighting its low-cost asset-light payment model that bypasses traditional card networks and its fast, accessible real-time transfer capabilities.
key_points: Cuts expensive credit card fees by bypassing existing card networks
Uses a $.25/transaction fee model and offers free micro-transactions under $10
Pre-loaded funds move in real time, outperforming physical checks
Features FiSync Technology as the first real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system in the US
Accessible for use with any web-enabled device

slides.transcript:
THE DWOLLA NETWORK

SAFER & PRIVACY FOCUSED
- Guards sensitive financial information, never discloses this data inside transactions or devices.
- Privacy innovations, like "Add/Remove Features" revoke access to third-party applications

OPEN-LOOP & END-TO-END
- Dwolla API allows distributes network and third-party innovation
- With FiSync, Dwolla streamlines payments from user bank account-to-user bank account
- Agnostic to payment type (i.e. p2p, b2b, c2b, b2c, g2b, b2g, etc.) or hardware

BANK-FRIENDLY, CONSUMER-CENTRIC
- FiSync provides banks and credit unions with dynamic value-added product and services opportunities
slides.summary: This slide outlines the core features and architecture of the Dwolla Network, highlighting its safety, privacy controls, open-loop system, end-to-end capabilities, and bank-friendly integration.
key_points: Guards sensitive financial information by never disclosing it inside transactions or devices
Offers privacy innovations like 'Add/Remove Features' to revoke access to third-party applications
Features a Dwolla API that allows a distributed network and third-party innovation
Streamlines bank-to-bank payments using FiSync and remains agnostic to payment type or hardware
Provides banks and credit unions with dynamic value-added product and services opportunities via FiSync
